newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU waits for U.S. response on meat deal.
newsitem.headline: EU waits for U.S. response on meat deal.

text.p: European Union officials said on Monday they were waiting to hear from the United States about a tentative deal to end a three-year dispute over meat imports.
Officials said a letter indicating the extent of agreement was expected to be delivered to the European Commission in Brussels before a Tuesday deadline set by Washington for an accord to be reached.
At issue is a long-standing dispute between the two sides over veterinary inspections of imported animal products.
On April 1, the 15-nation EU introduced new rules which U.S. officials say block about $100 million-worth of U.S. exports to Europe.

The new rules were introduced after the failure of the two sides to reach agreement in talks which began after the end of the Uruguay Round of negotiations under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade three years ago.
EU officials said agreement was close for all products concerned except poultry. The EU has objected to the U.S. practice of sterilising finished poultry meat with hyper-chlorinated water.
The officials said the question at hand was whether the U.S. would accept an agreement for everything except poultry, or alternatively a deal allowing for a six-month transition period.

If no agreement is reached by Tuesday, Washington has said it intends to remove over 100 European meat and poultry plants from its list of approved exporters. That action could halt up to $300 million worth of EU meat shipments to the United States, mostly pork products from Denmark and ham from Italy.
U.S. and EU officials met in Washington last week to try to work out a deal in the so-called verterinary equivalency talks.
